svg.text: Multi-DB v2 — executing a decomposed question: per sub-query the databases are selected FIRST, then the sub-query is interpreted for them, then fetched in parallel
"For genes linked to Parkinson's disease — which drugs target them, and are those drugs approved?"
breaks the multi-intent question into ordered sub-queries — a dependency DAG (later sub-queries use earlier results)
— the orchestrator runs the SAME 4-step cycle once per sub-query (3 iterations shown unrolled, left → right)
pick DBs for the relation disease → gene
parse sub-query for the chosen DBs' schema
3 fan-out — query the selected DBs in parallel ▼
each = single-DB pipeline · run in parallel
gene list: SNCA, LRRK2, PRKN, PINK1 …
pick DBs for the relation gene → drug
parse for chosen DBs + inject Step-1 genes
3 fan-out — query the selected DBs in parallel ▼
multiple DBs answer the SAME sub-query
pick DBs for the relation drug → approval
parse for chosen DBs + inject Step-2 drugs
3 fan-out — query the selected DBs in parallel ▼
DB set differs per sub-query & intent
joins all sub-answers into the final result set — cross-links genes → drugs → approval across every database
The loop, in words — how a decomposed answer is built
The orchestrator takes each sub-query in DAG order and runs ONE four-step cycle:
1 Select DBs — pick every database whose scope fits the sub-query's relation → 2 Interpret the sub-query into those DBs' structured filter
→ 3 Fan-out — fetch from the selected databases IN PARALLEL (each runs its own single-DB pipeline) → 4 Merge their rows into one sub-answer
DBs are chosen BEFORE the interpreter runs — the interpreter must parse the sub-query against the selected databases' schema. Resolved
entities carry into the next sub-query, so the cycle repeats. Then the Aggregator + Synthesizer / Critic produce the final answer.
